Vier-Anderle is a simple trick-taking tarock game suitable for gambling, played in the vicinity of Furtwangen in the Black Forest in Germany. A similar game is played in the region around Offenburg under the name Strassenwart. The rules were recorded by Nick Wedd, who learned the game from Walter Strunz. It belongs to the Rams group of trick-taking games and uses the Cego pack with pip cards removed.
38-card Cego pack. 22 tarocks (GstieÃŸ=highest to 1). Suits: Black K-Q-Kt-J, Red K-Q-Kt-J.
The cards are dealt clockwise, with each player receiving four cards. Vorhand (the player on the dealer's left) leads to the first trick; the winner of each trick leads to the next.
